sections.heading: A new leader on the board
sections.text: Yi-Chia Chen leads the ARC-AGI-3 public board at 71.48, ahead of Tufa Labs at 68.91. An observed score event moved her from 68.21 to 71.48, a gain of 3.27, and took her from second to first. sections.heading: The chase behind them
sections.text: Team Turducken holds third at 56.02, unchanged. The last dance moved from fifth to fourth in the same overnight window, rising from 49.85 to 50.69 and passing mtg, which slips to fifth at 50.37 with no change in score. Grigoriy Zatravkin, 復活の混テキスト, NVARC3, artificialagencylab.com and Majkel1337 follow in sixth through tenth, all unchanged from the previous close.

sections.heading: The gold line tightens
sections.text: Gold places on the public board run through 19th, with the provisional line at 38.22, up 0.02 from the previous close. yktori gained 6.74 to reach 42.77, climbing from 42nd to 11th in a recorded overnight move. fshindo, at 38.20 and unchanged, slipped from 19th to 20th and sits 0.02 short of the line. Jan Disselhoff rose 0.21 over its recent comparison window to 38.58 and holds 18th, inside the gold places, while Lord Han Solo is 29th at 37.07. Medal places are provisional until the private standings are final.

discussionThreads.reason: New substantive participant experiments and negative results; signed-in body/reply read, then verified readable without login.
discussionThreads.summary: Francise Liang reports stopping work and shares tests of Franzen’s public Milestone 2 notebook on an RTX Pro 6000, with 25 public games and two passes per run. Two unchanged runs averaged 47.30 and 48.92; per-game differences had a reported standard deviation of 24 points. Increasing concurrent streams from ten to fourteen reduced the reported mean from 47.30 to 29.90 and throughput; stopping stalled levels at 110k tokens gave 38.97 versus a two-run baseline average of 48.11. Liang recommends repeated comparisons. These are participant measurements on public games, not independently reproduced results or hidden-board scores. Reply author xiaoz259 attributes poor throughput to insufficient KV-cache memory and lane preemption.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize reports verified Reflection Beam 1.0 scores: ARC-AGI-2 23.5% at $0.61/task and ARC-AGI-1 74.0% at $0.31/task. Best scores use xhigh reasoning; high reaches 20.0% on ARC-AGI-2 at about 43% lower cost.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: New official model evaluation. Linked result page independently read in Chrome: semi-private best scores match. This is benchmark evaluation, not a Kaggle team score.

socialPosts.author: alin8020
socialPosts.summary: Alan Lin discusses the previously published ARC-AGI-3 standard/provider-adapter results and argues that retaining reasoning between steps matters when choosing a harness.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Fresh public commentary on existing results. Treat as Lin’s interpretation, not a new evaluation or proof that reasoning retention alone caused the difference.

socialPosts.author: gklambauer
socialPosts.summary: Klambauer announces KronLSTM and links the new Kronecker Delta Rule paper. The authors propose a targeted association update for recurrent linear attention, report competitive long-context performance, and link open-source code and models. No ARC score is reported.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Research lead discovered in fses91’s separate Reposts feed. The primary arXiv abstract was checked independently; architecture claims remain attributed, and no Kaggle roster identity is inferred.

socialPosts.whyItMatters: Keeps the cost basis and absence of ARC-AGI-3 results explicit.

socialPosts.author: arcprize

socialPosts.whyItMatters: Primary follow-up with reproducibility and policy links; group with the Beam announcement.

socialPosts.summary: Replying to Psyho’s PuzzleScript benchmark announcement, Barry says Epoch might be able to support API costs and that he has sent a DM. This is a tentative public statement; no funding agreement or collaboration is established.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: New response to the archive’s independent benchmark lead; recheck any later public confirmation before describing support as secured.

socialPosts.whyItMatters: Organizer interest in an independent game benchmark; the message contents and any collaboration are unknown.
